source_snapshot.test_name_items: SOL console - in OS condition and output OS log, keyboard type check
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    *This section will cover the configuration of serial terminals in Ubuntu. Different OS may have different configuration for redirecting the serial console output to the SOL
1. Modify /etc/default/grub
     GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=“consol=tty0 console=ttyS1,115200n8” 
     GRUB_TERMINAL=console 
     GRUB_SERIAL_COMMAND=“serial --unit=0 --speed=115200 --word=8 --parity=no --stop=1”
2. Run “update-grub” command to make it work
     #sudo update-grub
3. After configuring and reboot the system, you can operate the system via SOL.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. SOL console should show the log info during boot up, also can see the OS screen (include OS log).
2. Keyboard should type in any key and respond correctly.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- not runnable by agent: the "SOL console in OS condition" check requires opening an SOL serial-console session and typing keyboard input on the live Linux console; the agent cannot operate the interactive serial console terminal.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator opens the SOL console, types on the OS console and reads the OS log output; agent cannot drive the interactive serial terminal.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO recognizes the interactive SOL boundary, but incorrectly treats all terminal automation as unavailable and does not address the source's `consol=tty0` typo, platform-specific ttyS1 assumption, bootloader mutation, reboot, authentication, safe command scope or rollback.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED correctly requires OS-specific serial mapping, configuration backup, approval and a safe marker. V3.1 reclassifies the evidence and bounded console-input portion as package-capable while preserving human approval for bootloader changes, reboot, WebUI/session observation and verdict.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 910/2291 retains NO/physical status and generic operator evidence without validating GRUB syntax, actual kernel console device, getty/login path, BMC SOL parameters, linked Script revision or restoration.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The preceding BIOS-stage SOL case does not establish OS bootloader/getty coverage. SSH, KVM and post-hoc host logs do not prove the BMC SOL path or live keyboard transport.

historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the Ubuntu example and internal Script reference; ED-34 treats OS/bootloader/serial parameters as Project readiness inputs; ED-35 prevents replacing interactive SOL with passive logs; ED-38 requires approval for mutation/reboot, one attempt, recovery and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC SOL console for the intended SUT carries attributable OS boot/runtime output and correctly transports bounded keyboard input to the live OS console after an OS-appropriate serial-console configuration.
original_method: Determine the actual OS, bootloader, UART and SOL mapping; if serial redirection is not already enabled, back up and apply an engineer-approved OS-specific configuration, validate the generated boot configuration, reboot once in the approved window, capture the SOL boot/runtime stream, exercise a harmless authenticated marker, then close SOL and restore temporary configuration as planned.
manual_activity: An engineer approves any bootloader/serial change and reboot, validates the actual UART/getty mapping and recovery access, and selects the safe authenticated input. A human may open or visually supervise the supported SOL client. Automation can back up and validate configuration, capture the stream, send a bounded marker and correlate logs, but cannot authorize mutation/reboot or declare the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT, OS image, kernel, bootloader and firmware identities plus current host state
Actual UART and Linux device mapping, SOL channel/payload and complete serial parameters
Supported OS-specific serial-console and getty configuration; source ttyS1 example is not universal
Pinned reviewed internal Script revision or explicit decision not to use it
Backups, hashes, syntax/generation checks and local/out-of-band rollback access
Maintenance and single-reboot approval with independent recovery observer
Approved SOL client/account and safe OS test account/marker command
Expected boot, kernel, init, getty/login and runtime markers with timing/loss thresholds
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC, SOL, OS journal, boot or audit logs; preserve the pre-change baseline and first-failure evidence.
Do not copy `ttyS1`, unit 0, 115200n8 or the misspelled `consol=tty0` into a live bootloader configuration without Project/OS validation.
Back up exact configuration and rendered bootloader output, validate syntax and maintain an independent recovery path before any approved write or reboot.
Obtain point-of-action approval for configuration change and reboot; perform one planned attempt and do not blindly retry on missing output or boot failure.
Do not type credentials into an ambiguous prompt, expose them in captures or execute destructive/root commands. Use an approved non-destructive marker in a constrained account.
Stop on wrong-target session, garbled output, unexpected prompt, boot failure, repeated/dropped input or lost recovery path; close SOL and use the approved rollback.
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, actual UART/SOL/getty mapping, OS-supported configuration, reviewed Script revision, backup/rollback, reboot approval and evidence contract.

After approval, assist with read-only baseline and configuration diff/syntax validation; present writes and the one reboot for explicit human confirmation rather than applying generic source values blindly.
Capture timestamped SOL boot/runtime output, correlate kernel/init/getty/login markers and send only the approved harmless marker or command at an authenticated prompt.
Verify final configuration/host state, archive raw/redacted evidence and stop without log clear, destructive input, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the actual serial device and OS/bootloader/getty configuration, including whether the source example or internal Script is applicable.
Approve backups, change/reboot window, safe account/marker, acceptance thresholds and independent rollback/recovery path.
Supervise state changes and live-console boundary, review output/input/restoration evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The no-command decision is valid for an environment limited to host SSH, but approved SOL clients can automate capture and bounded input. DeepSeek omits the risk of blindly applying the source's typo and ttyS1-specific GRUB example.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the selected OS's supported bootloader/serial-console procedure and an approved SOL client. Generate exact commands only after UART, bootloader and Project inputs are supplied; require human confirmation for writes and reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Ubuntu example, `/etc/default/grub`, `consol=tty0`, ttyS1/115200n8, `update-grub`, reboot, SOL keyboard/log Criteria, internal Script URL, DeepSeek NO and 5/5-minute estimates remain preserved as source evidence, not universal safe commands.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Discover and validate the real serial path, back up and apply only an approved OS-specific configuration if needed, reboot once, capture all SOL boot/runtime stages and verify a harmless authenticated input, then restore per plan.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC SOL implementation and SUT OS/kernel/bootloader/UART/getty configuration.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, OS image, kernel, bootloader tools, init/getty, SOL client and configuration revision.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: OS/kernel serial-console and bootloader documentation, BMC vendor SOL specification, Project console policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains the OS SOL purpose while replacing blind generic example use with discovered mapping, reviewed syntax, backup, bounded input and rollback controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: SSH or host-collected logs do not prove SOL transport; boot output alone does not prove authenticated runtime input; an alternate client does not automatically prove the source WebUI path.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Actual serial/OS mapping, reviewed procedure, approval, backup/rollback, expected markers and safe input.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong console parameter can hide boot output or impair boot access; reboot and live shell input are state-changing; captures may expose credentials or sensitive logs.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor/IPMI SOL client or an OS-specific bootloader tool instead of the example only when the source values, actual values, reason, engineering approval, equivalent output/input coverage and rollback are recorded. Passing an alternate client does not claim the original WebUI path passed; a preconfigured console may omit the mutation checkpoint but must preserve baseline evidence.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/OS/kernel/bootloader identities, current host state, actual UART/SOL/getty parameters and reviewed Script/procedure revision
Pre-change configuration and generated-output backup/hash, approved diff, syntax validation, reboot authorization and independent recovery readiness
Timestamped SOL capture spanning bootloader, kernel, init/getty, authenticated login/runtime and required OS log markers
Safe keyboard marker/command with prompt identity, sent/received text, latency, drop/repeat/garble and reconnect observations
Post-test configuration diff/restoration, host/BMC state, preserved BMC/SOL/OS logs, client/WebUI coverage difference and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently target OS-stage SOL output and keyboard input. The misspelled `consol`, ttyS1/unit assumptions and OS-specific syntax are clear source defects/readiness hazards but do not create competing test purposes; they must be preserved and corrected only in the Review/Project layer.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The OS SOL purpose is clear. Project/OS discovery can supply the serial mapping, supported configuration, safe input, reboot approval and recovery plan, so missing inputs are readiness pending rather than permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes blanket NO to PACKAGE for automatable configuration checks, SOL capture and bounded input, while retaining approval/manual boundaries and rejecting SSH substitution.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Builds on its backup and safe-marker controls, explicitly preserves the source typo and internal Script, requires generated-config validation and reclassifies only the automatable portion.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic operator photos with exact configuration provenance, multi-stage console markers, per-input evidence and rollback verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps BIOS-stage SOL, KVM and SSH coverage separate from this OS console path.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents a misspelled or wrong-port GRUB example from being applied blindly and prevents SSH/log evidence from being reported as live SOL keyboard coverage, while preserving useful safe automation around configuration validation and transcript capture.
independent_technical_reasoning: OS SOL spans several independent layers: BMC payload/channel, physical UART, kernel console, bootloader terminal, init/getty and authentication. A stream can show one layer while another is broken. Because these layers are machine-readable, much evidence can be automated, but modifying boot configuration, rebooting and interacting with a live prompt require approved inputs, recovery and human ownership. That makes this a hybrid package rather than inherently manual-only.
